labels.notes: Unmarked and reported partial, which is right: the existence half ("this remark does not extend") is the tagged sorry GX.exists_positive_negative. (i) GX.rp1Iso_of_zpowers_eq says exactly what l.927-928 says. Lifted holonomy is defined only up to conjugacy and HasLiftedHolonomy is closed under conjugation (IsLiftedDevPair.conj), so 'L has holonomy <g>' means some representative f has <f> = <g>, which is the Lean hypothesis. (ii) GX.conj_inv_swaps_timelike_spacelike: h in G~ with h g h^-1 = g^-1, g the lift with a fixed point of A != 1 in Gamma_p, p in dS2. h sends time-like directions to space-like ones and space-like to time-like, which is at least l.928-930. It rests on IPm's time-like reading of i^+-, OQ-116 (a), and the checklist discloses that. Here g lifts the holonomy factor because k is even (even_of_nonneg). (iii) GX.not_isIso_of_positive_of_negative holds in the disclosed reading of isomorphism as 'same p' (GammaLinkCircle.IsIso). Under that reading the negative conclusion is weaker than one where an SO0(1,2) element may move p; the checklist and the REPORT question name this. IsSpacelikePositive/Negative are not vacuous: spacelike_dichotomy shows every space-like circle of degree >= 1 is exactly one of the two, and the quotient examples exist mathematically (unbuilt, under the sorry). The definition is the paper's 'in other words' form (l.915), not its primary definition (l.908-913); see the minor finding. All three assertions use propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only. The paper block and its ledger row (colI_v1.tex:926, informal, bucket D) match the docstring's label line and its verbatim quote.

findings.what: False sub-claim in a finding sent to the author. The finding says 'Same for the time-like (central holonomy, e.g. the half-turn) ... cases. Smallest correction: with non-trivial holonomy', i.e. that l.788-791's 'L is an elliptic RP1-circle' also needs non-trivial holonomy. That is not a defect of the paper. At a time-like p the half-turn (GX.gammaHalfTurn, acting on l(p) as sigma -> -sigma) has lifted holonomy delta, and RP~1/<delta> is RP1 itself. l.693-694 names RP1 explicitly as an elliptic circle ('Observe that it includes the usual real projective structure on RP1'). The hub's reading OQ-113 (d), adopted by this file in SCOPE (b), counts central holonomy as elliptic. The file's own GX.GammaLinkCircle.IsLiftedDev.isElliptic_of_timelike (l.1961) states the time-like case with no non-trivial-holonomy hypothesis, while isHyperbolic_of_deSitter and isParabolic_of_null carry one. So the finding contradicts both the paper's text and the file. The dS2 and light-like parts of the finding are true: at p in dS2 or on the boundary of H2, Gamma_p contains no -id, so trivial Gamma_p-holonomy gives lifted holonomy delta^(2n), which is neither hyperbolic nor parabolic.
findings.fix: Drop 'the time-like (central holonomy, e.g. the half-turn) and' from the finding, so that it covers the space-like and light-like bullets only (l.794-795, l.797-800). Alternatively, state the time-like part only as conditional on rejecting OQ-113 (d), the strict reading of 'elliptic' that l.693-694 rules out.

findings.what: The finding's only Lean counterexample, GX.regular_not_isHyperbolic, is the link of a regular point. In e(l(p)) the point p is not singular, and the printed bullets classify singularities, so an author may dismiss the counterexample as outside the claim. The finding is still true for genuine singularities: the n-fold cyclic cover of l(p), n >= 2, has trivial Gamma_p-holonomy and lifted holonomy delta^(2n), central and not hyperbolic.
findings.fix: Add the n-fold cover (n >= 2) as the singular counterexample, argued or built, and say that regular_not_isHyperbolic covers the regular link.

findings.what: Several line citations are off. In colI_v1.tex the space-like bullet is l.794-795, but the file cites l.796-797, which is a blank line followed by the start of the light-like bullet. Time-like is l.788-791 (cited l.789-792). Light-like is l.797-800 (cited l.800-803). Positive/negative is l.908-915, the negative case l.911-913 (cited l.908-918, l.916-918). Light-like of degree >= 1 is l.917-922 (cited l.920-924). Findings go to the author with these numbers.

The checklist marks the row ✓, but IsSpacelikePositive/Negative formalize the paper's restatement at l.915 ('positive iff g x >= x on I+'). The paper's primary definition (l.908-913) is that the left extremities of the components of I+ are repelling fixed points of g. The equivalence of the two is true (through IsHyperbolic.fixed_structure and timelike_spacelike_dir) but is not formalized. Label (iii) rests on this definition.
findings.fix: Mark the row ⚠ (reading: the l.915 form, equivalence with l.908-913 argued) and add it to SCOPE, or prove the equivalence with GTilde.IsRepellingAt/IsAttractingAt.

findings.what: l.721-723 says the circles are isomorphic iff their 'holonomy groups are conjugate'. GX.rp1Iso_iff_conj uses conjugacy of the oriented lifted holonomies (elements), so its 'if' half has a stronger hypothesis than the group form. The group form follows from the canonical orientation (deg_nonneg, positivity of degree-0 parabolics, direction of elliptics, g ~ g^-1 for hyperbolics), but only its hyperbolic equal-group case is proved (rp1Iso_of_zpowers_eq). The row is reported 'closed ... iso<->conj' with no reading named. This is the paper's orientation-corrected form (l.723-731), so it is not a Lean < paper defect, but it is undisclosed.
findings.fix: Name the element reading in the prose row and the docstring, or add the group form (zpowers conjugate => iso) for every type.
